commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Clean failing uv caches safely (#9340)

Install Iris-managed uv environments with clone mode so cache cleanup
cannot
invalidate running tasks. On an existing CoreWeave node, the task
workdir and
shared cache were on the same XFS filesystem with reflinks enabled. A
1.237 GB
locked environment installed from a warm cache in a median 260.5 ms with
clone
mode, versus 176.5 ms with symlinks. Clone-installed environments
survived
`uv cache clean`; symlink-installed environments did not. The
[benchmark and design
record](https://loom.oa.dev/s/ap6dmu49/artifacts/uv-cache-recovery-proposal)
contains the concurrent results and reproduction details.

Keep the shared cache as the default and retry a failed setup-time
install once
with a task-local cache. After the local retry succeeds, the task setup
wrapper
writes an attempt-UID marker into the node's `/uv/cache`. Three distinct
markers
on one node within 30 minutes make the node agent run `uv cache clean`
against
that shared cache. The agent emits `uv_cache_recovery_observed` when it
consumes
a marker and `uv_cache_cleared` after a successful clean.

The generic age-based reclaimer skips `/uv/cache`. Cache mutation there
runs
through uv's cache command and lock. The node agent now runs on every
Kubernetes
task node with the cache hostPath mounted, so it can see recovery
markers when
Finelog and age-based reclamation are disabled.

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Drop dead FA4 index helper, coverage validator, and log guards (#9325)

`iris.runtime.telemetry.configure` and the controller's native-proxy
metrics
poller each wrapped their `logger.warning` call in a second
`try/except Exception: pass`. `logging` routes handler and formatting
failures
through `Handler.handleError` instead of raising, so the inner guard
could only
discard the warning the outer handler exists to emit. A failure to
configure
Finelog telemetry or to read a native-proxy snapshot is now always
reported.
`configure` also ended with a `return` after the final statement.

`_packed_segment_backward_block_sparse_indices` in the FA4 CUTE backend
merged
the partial and full Q-block metadata into one index list. The backward
pass has
consumed `_packed_segment_backward_block_sparse_indices_with_full`
directly since
D128 GQA moved to SM90 in 587d6e16bf, leaving the merge reachable only
from its
own test. Both are deleted; the remaining tests still cover the
`_with_full`
partial/full split and the causal lower bounds the metadata is built
from.

`_validated_coverage` in `marin.evaluation.lm_eval_samples` has had no
caller
since #9145. `BenchmarkMetadataRef.validate_protocol` rejects
`n_attempted > n_benchmark` and constrains both counts to be
non-negative, and
`task_coverage_and_metrics` raises when the sample document extent
exceeds
`n_attempted` before it builds the coverage record.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Enable context-parallel hero training (#9119)

Shard the hero residual stream by sequence and keep parameters and Muon
state partitioned across the context group, including the expert bank
when only the context axis splits it. Route each context shard
independently and preserve global router statistics. Configure the
trainer batch mesh for 262K-token sequences at batch size 16 on EP16 x
CP4, and derive optimizer scaling from the actual sequence length.

Expose sequence, mesh, attention-scale, and checkpoint overrides in
diagnostic launchers while retaining the production defaults. Reject an
expert bank that the expert and context axes together cannot split
before the fleet is allocated. Cap small-model evaluation batches at the
training batch size. Runs with at least 256 training sequences per step
retain the existing evaluation batch size of 256.

The earlier benchmark revision (`b5c7f84ff6`, before the review fixes)
completed 40 updates on 64 GB200s at a 262K-token sequence length, with
10.03% median MFU and 1.42% mean dropped assignments:
https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc-main-ragged-262k-0911.
This throughput measurement does not establish long-context training
quality.

Stacked on #9118.

Part of #8754

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Keep length-1 mesh axes in the FA4 output sharding (#9346)

FA4/CuTe attention now returns Q's own partition spec, including mesh
axes of length 1. Since #9117 the wrapper dropped those axes from its
output spec. Explicit sharding compares axis names, so on a mesh where a
batch axis has length 1 the model's gating multiply rejects the
attention output with a ShardingTypeError at trace time. The hero mesh
(11 racks x EP64) has data=1 and fails this way on main; the
context-parallel meshes in #9119 also have data=1.

The new hero-model test traces the loss and gradient through the FA4
wrapper, with the CUDA kernel replaced, on meshes with and without a
length-1 data axis. It fails on main with the ShardingTypeError and
passes with this change. The real kernel was not run.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Cache repeated bounded log tails (#9347)

Cache initial bounded `FetchLogs` tail results by the full normalized
filter and advance cached snapshots with sequence-bounded delta scans.
On a hub catalog with 6.71 billion rows in 715 objects, a repeated
100-line tail for source prefix `/muchanem/glm53-relay-e/` containing
`routes:` fell from a 1.309-second median to 65 milliseconds (20.1x)
with identical rows and cursor. The first request after the Finelog hub
restart took 2.685 seconds; subsequent unchanged-snapshot requests took
50–76 milliseconds.

Coalesce concurrent disk loads of identical immutable `.fidx` bundle
headers or parsed index sections. Report cache occupancy, load attempts,
coalesced waits, and evictions through `/api/server`. Slow `Query` and
`FetchLogs` warnings now separate visibility waits, provider
construction, logical planning, physical planning, execution,
normalization, and response encoding.

Use disjoint metric-name branches and separate lookback windows in the
hero-health and training-stall alert queries. This retains 24-hour phase
and evaluation liveness history while bounding health metrics to 65
minutes and progress metrics to 30 minutes.

Detailed diagnosis and benchmark protocol: [Finelog slow-query diagnosis
and 10x execution
plan](https://loom.oa.dev/s/6twmncpa/artifacts/finelog-slow-query-plan).

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[eval] Isolate external judge credentials (#9197)

FinanceBench launches now keep an external judge endpoint, model, and
`SecretSpec` credential separate from candidate authentication. The
checked-in FinanceBench and SimpleQA policies use Together's
`openai/gpt-oss-120b` judge and resolve its provider credential through
the local environment or the managed cloud source. Records retain the
judge endpoint and model while omitting credential references and
values. URLs with credentials, query strings, or fragments fail during
config validation.

Current main pins include the strict FinanceBench and SimpleQA graders
from Evalchemy #130 and Harbor #154. FinanceBench accepts only exact
grader labels and propagates judge transport failures without producing
scores. SimpleQA version 1.1 selects the corrected generated dataset
through the registry at the current Harbor pin and applies the same
failure semantics to all 4,326 tasks.

Loopback OpenAI-compatible servers verified distinct fake judge
credentials at both evaluator boundaries. The 89 focused tests and the
affected Marin suite of 1,960 tests pass. No paid provider or cluster
evaluation was run.

Fixes #9070

Example job:
https://iris.oa.dev/#/job//karan/eval-20260922-195827-qwen3-0.6b-ea18

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[eval] Score aggregate-only Evalchemy tasks by enumerated documents (#9156)

Evalchemy's AIME24 and OlympiadBench grade the whole item set and write
only an
aggregate `accuracy_avg`; their sample rows carry no per-item score. The
export
previously recorded zero scored items, so the panel rejected these runs
with
"no item count."

Count every enumerated document as scored when evaluator metadata
declares an
aggregate `_avg` primary metric. Scoreless rows for ordinary benchmarks
remain
ungraded, so incomplete or historical sample files cannot report full
coverage. Aggregate-scored tasks have no per-item pass tally.

This uses the benchmark protocol added by #9145. A capped AIME24 run
remains
ineligible under the benchmark coverage gate. The behavior was verified
against the pinned Evalchemy fork's sample-row shape; no stored AIME24
record
was available.

[inference] Guard tool loops, preserve XML, and share chats (#9337)

Default chat tool exchanges to unlimited rounds and expose a persisted

The UI stops before executing a third consecutive call with the same

Add short share links backed by bounded, process-local snapshots. Links

capability URL, which grants endpoint access until the Iris-assigned

[levanter] Support context-parallel short convolution (#9118)

Exchange the left neighbor's activations and segment IDs before running the local convolution, then discard halo outputs. This preserves causal values and gradients across sequence shards for the reference and Pallas backends. Reject halos larger than one shard's local sequence length because the exchange reads only the adjacent shard. The context-parallel path keeps the channel-axis guard of the unsharded path, so a channel dimension partitioned across multiple "model" shards raises instead of being silently all-gathered when resharding for the local convolution.

Share partition inspection between the convolution and Grug through levanter.sharding. Preserve concrete arrays' placement on JAX Auto mesh axes and empty partition specs; Grug callers still select default token sharding for empty specs.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Use shared uv cache until setup fails (#9330)

Keep every task attempt on the node-shared uv cache. During setup, Iris
wraps `uv sync` and `uv pip install`: the first failed install retries
against `$IRIS_WORKDIR/.uv-recovery-cache` with `--reinstall`, and a
workdir marker keeps later installs in that attempt on the recovery
cache. Other uv commands are not replayed because their exit status may
come from user code. Retries caused by workload or infrastructure
failures no longer force a cold dependency sync.

In-place cache cleaning remains unsafe while Iris virtual environments
symlink to cached files. The [repair
proposal](https://loom.oa.dev/s/0nkqy1cf/artifacts/uv-cache-recovery-proposal)
compares copy and clone modes with cache-generation quarantine, then
outlines cache-owner detection, rotation, telemetry, and reclamation.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Add context mesh support and preserve token shard reductions (#9116)

Add a context axis to the Grug mesh while preserving parameter placement
at context degree one. Read token partitioning from traced arrays so MoE
drop-count reductions count each dropped assignment once and fused loss
retains sequence sharding instead of gathering activations.
Expert-parallel MoE rejects a token partition that omits the expert
axis, since its shard_map follows the input spec and would otherwise
hand every expert rank the same tokens.

Variants without sequence sharding reject context parallelism during
configuration. Legacy checkpoints can restore onto the new mesh with
parameters partitioned across expert and context axes.

Part of #8754

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Recover task setup and serving failures (#9322)

On the first task attempt, Iris starts `uv sync` against the node-shared
cache. A failed default sync retries within that attempt against
`$IRIS_WORKDIR/.uv-recovery-cache` and reinstalls the environment. The
attempt workdir persists through the run command, so the new symlink
targets remain valid.

Each scheduler retry after attempt zero sets
`UV_CACHE_DIR=$IRIS_WORKDIR/.uv-cache` before any setup script runs.
Default and custom scripts therefore avoid a malformed entry from the
node-shared cache on later attempts. Only the generated default setup
script has the additional same-attempt fallback. Python installations
continue to use the shared cache.

Every `ZephyrContext` now gives its coordinator 1 CPU and 4 GiB of
memory unless the caller supplies `coordinator_resources`. The previous
0.1 CPU and 1 GiB default let full-workspace dependency setup exceed the
pod memory limit before the coordinator actor registered. CoreWeave
smoke runs
[35716738886](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/35716738886)
and
[35720717255](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/35720717255)
reproduced the `OOMKilled` setup failure and integration-test timeout.

Drafting-evaluation jobs also failed with `Metadata field Name not
found` while reading cached NumPy or pandas wheels. The workdir caches
avoid those node-shared entries. Direct and brokered remote-inference
jobs now set Iris `max_task_failures` to their configured
`max_retries_failure`, which defaults to one. The old cumulative budget
of zero ended the job on its first hard task failure before the per-task
replacement could run; a second hard failure now ends a
default-configured job and returns control to its parent pipeline.

Incident record: https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/499

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[inference] Add Git-aware Chat workspaces (#9263)

Give vLLM Chat workspaces ShellSim's current local Git behavior,
including branches, commits, merges, stashes, rebases, blame, and
reflog. Pin ShellSim to the reviewed upstream revision that provides
these operations.

Public GitHub imports now perform one credential-free shallow clone when
the user chooses **Clone public repo**. The service translates up to 32
recent first-parent commits and their bounded UTF-8 text changes into
ShellSim-native commits, then deletes the temporary clone. Models can
inspect prior revisions with `git log`, `git show`, `git diff`, and `git
blame` without subsequent network access.

The simulated workspace remains network-isolated, so clone, fetch, pull,
and push are unavailable during model tool calls. Imports exclude merge
topology, tags, submodules, binary and oversized files, private
repositories, and history outside the configured bounds.
